Standard Library > string: ASCII / UTF-8 Strings

string: ASCII / UTF-8 Strings

This page lists the extern functions in sa_std/string.sai, and the string macro family provided by sa_std/string.sa. After reading it, you will be able to tell whether a string is ASCII, count and traverse UTF-8 characters, and do case-insensitive comparison and concatenation.

extern Functions (from string.sai)

SignatureDescription
sa_str_is_ascii(ptr: ptr, len: u64) -> i32Whether a byte sequence is entirely ASCII
sa_str_eq_ignore_ascii_case(left: ptr, left_len: u64, right: ptr, right_len: u64) -> i32Compare ignoring ASCII case
sa_str_trim_ascii_start_index(ptr: ptr, len: u64) -> u64Compute the starting index after trimming leading whitespace
sa_str_trim_ascii_end_len(ptr: ptr, len: u64) -> u64Compute the length after trimming trailing whitespace
sa_str_utf8_char_count(ptr: ptr, len: u64) -> u64Count UTF-8 characters
sa_str_utf8_validate(ptr: ptr, len: u64) -> i32Validate UTF-8 well-formedness
sa_str_utf8_char_at(ptr: ptr, len: u64, char_index: u64, out_codepoint: ptr) -> i32Get a code point by character index
sa_str_utf8_char_at_byte(ptr: ptr, len: u64, byte_index: u64, out_codepoint: ptr, out_len: ptr) -> i32Get a character by byte index (code point + encoding length)
sa_str_utf8_lossy_next(ptr: ptr, len: u64, byte_index: u64, out_codepoint: ptr, out_len: ptr) -> i32Get the next character starting at a byte index, treating invalid sequences lossily
sa_str_utf8_char_range_at(ptr: ptr, len: u64, char_index: u64, out_start: ptr, out_len: ptr) -> i32Get the byte range of the nth character
sa_string_concat(left: ptr, left_len: u64, right: ptr, right_len: u64) -> u64Concatenate two byte spans, returning an owned buffer handle

SA Macros (string.sa, Excerpt)

string.sa is the implementation carrier for the Sla String/str method surface; common macros include:

MacroDescription
STR_LEN %out_len, %slice_regGet the length
STR_PTR / STR_AS_PTR %out_ptr, %slice_regGet the data pointer
STR_IS_EMPTY %out_bool, %slice_regWhether it is empty
STR_FROM_PARTS %out_slice, %data_ptr, %lengthBuild a slice from a pointer + length
STR_FROM_CONST %out_slice, %const_label, %const_lenBuild a slice from a constant label (alloc/string.sa)
STRING_NEW %out_sliceCreate a new mutable String
STR_TRY_FROM_UTF8 / STR_FROM_UTF8 %out_ok, %out_slice, %bytes_sliceBuild from a byte array, with validation / without validation
STR_AS_BYTES %out_slice, %slice_regConvert to a byte view

Byte / Text Conventions (TS-9, Written 2026-10-29)

SLA's String is a {ptr, len} byte handle: the type layer does not enforce a UTF-8 validity invariant, and it can hold arbitrary bytes. Construction that needs a text guarantee must go through the validating entry point str_from_utf8 (first validate with STR_IS_UTF8, then construct); there is also a self-describing unchecked construction path, which the caller uses at its own risk. String literals are naturally valid because the source is UTF-8.

The division of labour between bytes and text for the 25 externs in the string domain is as follows: the *_ascii family and the byte-operation family (concat, index_of, starts_with, ends_with, replace, pad, repeat) have pure byte semantics; the utf8_* family decodes by scalar — sa_str_utf8_validate explicitly validates well-formedness, sa_str_utf8_char_at returns a status code on error, sa_str_utf8_char_count returns 0 on an invalid sequence, and sa_str_utf8_lossy_next advances tolerantly over invalid sequences.

(Note: where Ord is provided for String at the SLA layer is still to be clarified (registered as TS-10); this section draws no conclusion.)

Example on the Sla Side

String comparison is used in Sla through str_eq. From the test in demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sla:

@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"
@import "sa_std/fmt.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

@test "rosetta 001 01_hello_world"() {
    if str_eq("hello, saasm", "hello, saasm") != true {
        panic(1);
    };
};
NoteAll sa_str_* functions accept a raw (ptr, len) rather than a string object; the owned buffer handle returned by sa_string_concat needs to be released explicitly.
